text:
riya: Quick finding from chaos run: when we do active-active with per-tenant residency, dual-commit can happen if routing cache invalidation lags. Small but important for compliance.

ben: Sequence? cache says region A owner, control-plane moved, but proxy still uses cached owner and accepts write?

riya: Yes. Client retries to A, write accepted locally, then owner-assertion fails later and sweep tries to move data. For customers with data residency flags that's a compliance leak.

anika: Can we add a fast invalidation hook on owner-change events to proxies? A short TTL + immediate push on change.

ben: Push works if control-plane emits events reliably. Need ack path so proxies can fail-closed if they miss invalidation.

infra-bot: deploy: pushed owner-change event streamer to staging at 1769400030 :white_check_mark:

riya: Proposal: per-tenant policy enum: enforce_strict | best_effort. enforce_strict => proxies reject writes when owner cache TTL expired or when they've missed a change (return 409). best_effort => allow smoothing.

anika: Also log and tag any retroactive sweeps with tenant id + reason. Makes audits easy.

ben: Action items: 1) add tenant policy flag to tenancy API (owner: ben) 2) implement push invalidation + proxy fail-closed hook (owner: anika) 3) add audit tagging for sweeps (owner: riya).

riya: I'll open the RFC with sequence diagram and compliance implications.

anika: I'll run a targeted chaos test after infra streamer lands.

ben: Sounds good. No objections.
